protocol.input: Unmodified publisher RescaleT(320) and ToTensorLab(flag=0), full original EXIF-oriented RGB. No corner, mask or ROI input.
protocol.target: Reviewed per-photo paper identity with unknown pixels excluded; synthetic original/scene/printed coverage from the same fixed 32 training geometries. Preserve fractional material coverage and source-pixel annotation uncertainty.
protocol.architecture: Freeze every parameter and buffer of the adapted U2NETP body. Reuse stage1d/2d/3d features through three 64-to-16 projections; combine with input RGB and frozen body scores in a two-layer 32-channel identity head at half resolution.
protocol.loss: Existing joint loss with one global A/B exchange per image. Frozen body loss is constant; only identity-head parameters receive gradients.
protocol.augmentation: Independent horizontal and vertical reflection of input and target together.
protocol.checkpointSelection: Final update only; no early stopping, held-out loss, alternative hyperparameters or per-photo checkpoint choices.
protocol.inference: Publisher body preprocessing and min/max normalization unchanged. Material is sigmoid of the second raw logit, with no per-image material min/max normalization.
protocol.evaluation: Verify unchanged body outputs and inspect all training predictions; then evaluate the fixed final head on the 32 source-separated development photographs. No checkpoint or per-photo winner selection.

scope: Paired development test of material colour input. Fresh raw control and body-relative treatment share the same initialized head, frozen body, 16 real photos, 96 synthetic views, draw/reflection schedule, 120 updates, optimizer, loss, inference threshold and evaluation cohort. No production changes.

comparison.validation: Require identical fresh initial heads, input tensor/label hashes and sampling schedules; exact preserved bodies. Inspect all real training and evaluation predictions. Controlled input feature tests check translation/common-scale invariance, finite constant inputs, and independent batch statistics. Training score alone cannot justify integration.
